scope: All 18 pseudo PNGs individually opened, 9 pages at 800x360 with safe insets and scales 100/200; code inspected, no tests/builds/devices/golden promotion.

issues.summary: Real native bootstrap resolves system to en-XA; ProductApp treats this as explicit English and disables pseudolocalization.
issues.detail: The renderer requires preference system plus Localizations en-XA. Native bootstrap sends the resolved tag; ProductController consumes it unchanged and ProductApp selects Locale(en) for non-zh non-system tags. New tests return system and capture uses Localizations.override, so they do not exercise native bootstrap semantics. Preserve/consume the raw preference separately and add an adapter-shaped bootstrap test.
issues.resolution: Both native bootstraps now expose raw localePreference; ProductController prefers it over resolved locale. Adapter-shaped en-XA/system regression covers the prior mismatch. Explicit locales and kDebugMode-only pseudo gating remain intact.

issues.summary: 200% wrapped hall toolbar clips the selected title and favorite hit area.
issues.detail: Selected title geometry is 136x112 at y160, but scroll viewport ends y232 (72px). PNG shows a partial second line. Favorite full geometry is 48x48 but visible semantic rect is 48x40. A two-line readable title and full 48px action must fit beside the 88px Continue button; exported full box checks alone do not detect this.
issues.resolution: Reopened corrected 200% hall PNG: both title lines fit, Favorite visible semantic height is 48 px, primary remains 88 px. In short large-text layouts categories use a horizontal strip with fixed tools; all four category controls remain in the scrollable strip. This is an acceptable compact-layout adaptation.

limits: No real OS en-XA activation evidence; capture explicitly overrides Localizations.
Search uses simulated IME insets, not system keyboard pixels.
Static captures do not prove every off-screen action can be reached; inspected vertical/horizontal scrolling structure and exported semantic actions.
Release debug-gating verified by source inspection, not release execution.
